claims.text: The mandatory step is not mandatory-and-ignored. Against a sim carrying a PERMANENT protected-field violation at tick 4000, the audit fails standalone (exit 1, '1 forbidden transient across 11902 ticks') AND the suite surfaces it: test_k03b_trajectory.py reported as '1 DEFECT — TRAJECTORY AUDIT FAILED'. Promoting a check to mandatory did not make it decorative.

The suite exit code flipped from 2 to 1. With the admission control still INCONCLUSIVE and the trajectory audit now failing, the suite reports exit 1 DEFECT rather than 2 — a real defect outranks an unrun check, exactly as the aggregation rule specifies. That rule was previously only exercised against synthetic stub tests; this is the first time it has been confirmed with a genuine failing check inside the real suite.

Under the dirty sim the canary check still passed — the audit caught its own planted transient at tick 3500 while separately reporting the permanent violation as a canonical failure. The two conditions are independent: a broken world does not disable the detector's self-test, and the detector reports both facts rather than collapsing them into one verdict.

risks: The violation is injected by patching a sandbox copy of the sim mirror, not by product code. This verifies the VERIFICATION PATH propagates a failure; it says nothing about whether the product can produce such a violation.

RX_ORACLE_DIR made this test easy, which also means a seat that sets it wrong gets a silently different sim. The audit exits 2 CANNOT EVALUATE when the mirror is missing, but it cannot detect a mirror that is present and wrong.
